items.title: COP31 opens in Türkiye with focus on implementation
items.one_liner: The UN climate summit COP31 opened in Antalya, focusing on climate finance and turning pledges into action.
items.why: Provides international policy context on climate finance, urban resilience, and global climate commitments.
items.action: Monitor COP31 outcomes regarding urban adaptation funding and Loss and Damage mechanisms.

items.title: TU/e researchers help cities use AI for resilient climate
items.one_liner: Researchers at Eindhoven University of Technology are helping cities use artificial intelligence for climate planning.
items.why: Connects with spatial modeling, scenario comparison, and advanced technical methods in urban planning.
items.action: Investigate the AI methodologies used to evaluate resilient climate futures in spatial planning.

items.title: UNFCCC COP31: Zero waste and resilient cities for Bangladesh
items.one_liner: Discussions at COP31 highlight zero waste, food security, and resilient cities for vulnerable nations like Bangladesh.
items.why: Highlights Global South urban vulnerabilities, food security, and resilience planning in semi-arid/delta settings.
items.action: Read the session briefs to compare adaptation strategies between South Asian urban contexts.

items.title: Urban Green Infrastructure Requires Strategic Pathways
items.one_liner: Research emphasizes that urban green infrastructure needs strategic pathways and governance for resilient cities.
items.why: Directly relates to urban ecosystem services, green-blue infrastructure, and environmental planning in cities.
items.action: Review the full research to extract governance strategies relevant to data-scarce urban settings.

items.title: Cities seek to build back better after climate shocks
items.one_liner: Cities are focusing on rebuilding and adapting following severe climate change shocks.
items.why: Informs research on urban climate resilience, adaptation, and ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction.
items.action: Examine case studies on post-shock recovery to integrate into scenario comparisons.

items.title: EIB provides €95.5M for water infrastructure in Hungary
items.one_liner: The European Investment Bank provides €95.5 million for climate-resilient water infrastructure upgrades.
items.why: Illustrates financing mechanisms for urban water management and annual water yield/stormwater retention.
items.action: Analyze how water infrastructure financing models can be adapted for data-scarce Global South cities.

note: Selected updates, not comprehensive coverage. Status is unverified unless supported by the quoted official excerpt.
